notes: Ports: 5985/tcp WinRM HTTP, 5986/tcp WinRM HTTPS, 135/tcp WMI.
name: WinRM / WMI - Enumeration & Access
description: WinRM (5985/5986) gives a remote PowerShell session with valid creds via evil-winrm; WMI (135) executes commands with Impacket's wmiexec.

defense.why_it_works: Adversaries scan for open ports and running services on network hosts to identify attack surface and potential exploitation targets. Tools like netcat, nmap, and service-specific clients probe for banner information that reveals software versions, which can then be matched against known vulnerabilities.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to WinRM (TCP 5985/5986); valid credentials for authenticated operations.
defense.impact: Remote system information and, with credentials, remote command execution.
defense.detection: Monitor for processes performing network enumeration by correlating process creation, socket connections, and sequential destination IP probing within a time window. Unusual port scanning patterns or banner-grabbing activity from internal hosts can indicate post-compromise discovery.
defense.artifacts: WinRM HTTP(S) requests and Windows logon events (4624) for the authenticating account.
defense.prevention: Close unnecessary ports and services to prevent risk of discovery and potential exploitation. Use network intrusion detection/prevention systems to detect and prevent remote service scans. Ensure proper network segmentation to protect critical servers and devices.
defense.misconfiguration: Services expose excessive information: version banners, supported auth methods, valid usernames via error responses. IPMI has no authentication (version 2.0 cipher 0 vulnerability). RSH/rexec trust .rhosts files. rsync shares readable anonymously. Oracle TNS allows remote poisoning in older versions.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# IPMI cipher 0 — no authentication required:
# ipmitool -H <ip> -U admin -P '' -I lanplus -C 0 chassis status
# Returns valid data — auth bypassed entirely

# rsync anonymous access:
# rsync --list-only rsync://<ip>/  # lists all modules without auth
# rsync rsync://<ip>/backup /tmp   # downloads backup files

# Oracle TNS — version banner reveals exact version:
# nmap -p 1521 -sV -> Oracle Database 11.2.0.4 (exact version)
defense.secure_config:
# IPMI — disable cipher 0, enable only strong ciphers:
# /etc/ipmi/ipmievd.conf: IPMI_CIPHER_SUITE=17  (AES, mandatory auth)
# Or disable IPMI entirely if not needed (BMC IPMI = critical attack surface)

# rsync — require auth:
# /etc/rsyncd.conf:
# [backup]
#   auth users = backupuser
#   secrets file = /etc/rsyncd.secrets
#   hosts allow = 10.10.1.0/24

# RSH/rexec — disable entirely (replaced by SSH):
systemctl disable rsh.socket rexec.socket rlogin.socket

# Oracle TNS — disable remote admin, enforce auth:
# sqlnet.ora: SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES = (BEQ, TCPS)  (not NONE)
